macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rebound as investors weigh persistent inflation
items.summary: The Dow rose 1.08% to 52,178.99, the S&P 500 gained 0.33% to 7,744.12, and the Nasdaq added 0.08% to 26,713.03. The move followed a volatile session in which hotter inflation initially pressured technology shares and lifted Treasury yields.[2]

items.title: September U.S. inflation raises rate-hike concerns
items.summary: U.S. headline inflation accelerated to 3.7% year over year in September from 3.4% in August, exceeding the 3.6% consensus estimate. Markets increased the implied probability of further Federal Reserve tightening, while the dollar strengthened and equities remained volatile.[8]

items.title: Bank earnings produce mixed results
items.summary: Bank of America fell 4.8% after reporting weaker-than-expected quarterly profit and revenue, while State Street declined 4.1% on disappointing revenue. Morgan Stanley and BlackRock exceeded expectations, but their shares had mixed reactions.[1][8]

items.title: Mortgage rates remain elevated
items.summary: The average U.S. 30-year fixed mortgage rate held at 7.4% for an eighth consecutive week, near its highest level since November 2023 and well above the 6.27% level recorded a year earlier.[2]

items.title: Asian technology shares face sharp volatility
items.summary: South Korea’s KOSPI fell about 8% at one point amid a global technology selloff, while concerns about AI-company debt and elevated valuations weighed on sentiment. TSMC nevertheless reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and indicated higher capital spending ahead.[6]

items.title: China reports stronger-than-expected trade surplus
items.summary: China’s trade surplus expanded to $133.53 billion in September from $119.09 billion in August, exceeding the $118.1 billion consensus estimate.[8]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,000 after inflation-driven sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell below $80,000 before recovering above $82,000, while Ethereum rebounded toward $2,400 and major altcoins also gained. More than $830 million in crypto positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, mostly longs, as hotter inflation increased expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike.[1]

items.title: Crypto market volatility intensifies amid U.S. inflation concerns
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped from roughly $83,700 to below $81,000 after U.S. inflation data lifted perceived odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike to 44%. The broader market reportedly lost $89 billion in capitalization, while nearly $1 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated and U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $261.4 million in net outflows on October 14.[2]

items.title: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs see continued outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of approximately $261.46 million, adding pressure to the market after the inflation-related decline. Bitcoin later recovered to around $82,400, with Ethereum near $2,457 and Solana near $106.[3]

items.title: FASB considers easing stablecoin accounting treatment
items.summary: A report from blockchain project Tempo said the U.S. Financial Accounting Standards Board is considering changes that could allow qualifying stablecoins to be treated as cash equivalents on corporate balance sheets. Such a change could reduce accounting barriers to business adoption.[4]

items.title: Gnosis updates bridge confirmations using Ethereum rule
items.summary: Gnosis said its xDAI Bridge and Omnibridge now use Ethereum’s Fast Confirmation Rule, allowing deposits to be confirmed in approximately one slot rather than waiting for full finality.[5]

items.title: New video game releases include Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse
items.summary: Several new games launched across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch and PC, including Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse. The roundup also covers Valor Mortis, Gears of War: E-Day and Forever Ago.

items.title: Bryson Tiller announces Brutal Industry game
items.summary: Musician Bryson Tiller revealed Brutal Industry, a beat-’em-up inspired by the music business. Trapsoul Games plans to release it in 2027, initially for Arcade1Up cabinets, with mobile and other platforms potentially following.

items.title: Arc System Works creates Tokyo Studio TAKUMI
items.summary: Arc System Works announced a new Tokyo development studio that will initially support a fighting game selected for Japan’s IP360 project. The project’s title, characters, platforms and release timing have not been disclosed.

items.title: Rockstar says GTA 6 development will accelerate future games
items.summary: Rockstar leadership reportedly said the engine, tools and team built for Grand Theft Auto 6 should speed up development of subsequent projects. GTA 6 is scheduled to launch on November 19, 2026.

items.title: Tales of Eternia Remastered launches in Japan
items.summary: Bandai Namco’s Tales of Eternia Remastered was reported as released, reviving the RPG’s adventure across the worlds of Inferia and Celestia.
